title: The Use of a Novel Porcine Derived Acellular Dermal Matrix (mucoderm®) in Peri-Implant Soft Tissue Augmentation: Preliminary Results of a Prospective Pilot Cohort Study
authors: Papi P. and Pompa G. Biomed Res Int. 2018 Jul 9;2018:6406051. doi: 10.1155/2018/6406051.
supports: Clinical study from the botiss mucoderm (porcine collagen soft-tissue matrix) literature list — the product featured in it, which is not the same as the study being about the product, so check the design and the comparator before citing it as product evidence. Authors' conclusion, verbatim: “The results of the present pilot study indicate that by placing a mucoderm® membrane during implant surgery the keratinized tissue width can be augmented, and the width remains stable for the assessment period of 12 months. Further studies with greater power and longer investigation period are needed to confirm the suggestion for clinical use” This records what the paper says, not what a rep may say: the sales wording still has to pass the claim tiers, and a study in one indication licenses nothing in another.
